docs.text: Welcome to Armskirk! ¶ Pick From the Visitor Brochure Rack ¶ Complimentary maps! Questionably complimentary advice! Take whatever catches your eye. Armskirk accepts no responsibility for missed trains, overconfident tour guides, regrettable haircuts requested by the customer, or anything a talking bird repeats under oath. Looking Presentable, Feeling Better ¶ Brochure What It Promises Cloud Mirror Salon — Adventure, Apology, or Court Appearance? Haircuts, hot-towel shaves, beard shaping, braids, fur brushing, feather oiling, horn polishing, and emergency repairs after helmets. Ask for Farrah Faucet. She already knows why you are here. Lotus Hot Springs Day Pass Madam Yu Zhen offers affordable public mineral baths, steam rooms, towels, scrubs, massage, laundry service, and neighborhood gossip at no additional charge. Jade Steam Private Onsen Reserved mineral baths, carved screens, flowering courtyards, tea service, and staff professionally trained not to notice the next room. All guests must leave before sunset; overnight accommodations and eight-armed employees are officially unavailable. Hundred Herbs Hall — Travel-Weary Remedies Affordable salves, combat tonics, monster oils, throwing powders, hangover remedies, and expert advice against drinking all of them at once. Ink Dragon Tattoo House Consultation Zhen “Calamity” Jian offers protective tattoos, family crests, spirit animals, moonlit ink, and questions suspiciously better than the answers. Silver Needle Tailors — Repairs While You Wait Travel-cloak relining, formal fittings, festival clothes, armor-friendly alterations, and new sleeves after the old ones met heroism. Saint Dacius Civic Hospital Charity Evening Healers, donors, speeches, light refreshments, and opportunities to look generous in public while supporting one of Leonia’s finest hospitals. Dr. Molar’s Miracle Mandibles Demonstration A live dental-strength exhibition promising teeth “strong enough to chew iron, soft enough for soup.” Dentists have requested we stop printing that sentence. Xiaolong: Food, Shopping, and Culture ¶ Brochure What It Promises Xiaolong: The Little Dragon District A lantern-lit walking route through tea houses, noodle shops, import markets, shrines, bathhouses, salons, and street food stalls. Xiaolong Night Market Tasting Pass Steamed buns, mooncakes, spicy skewers, rare teas, and at least one food item the brochure refuses to translate. Snake Blood Alley Delicacy Crawl Monster-part cuisine, chili oil, exotic broths, waiver forms in very small print, and a commemorative spoon for survivors. Golden Carp Tea House Ceremony Clementine Pekoe serves delicate teas, mooncakes, canal views, chess tables, and the usual order of customers who insist they have never visited. The old men are definitely not information brokers. Moon Gate Open-Air Theater Tonight: The Last Lantern at Eclipse Ford , a classic Mian wartime romance featuring seven farewells, one sunrise, Lincohn with an axe, and no refunds for crying. Thousand Feather Garden Aviary Jewel-plumed cranes, talking parrots, moon owls, thunderpheasants, and strict warnings not to repeat anything the birds say in court. White Crane Dojo — Visitor Lessons Master Shrew Fu teaches crane forms, tiger forms, flowing-river forms, and the beginner discipline of discovering how flexible you are not. Visitors may observe quietly or ache educationally. Little Dragon Shrine — Luck for the Road Incense, ribbons, tiny carved dragons, and a quiet place to ask for protection, honor an ancestor, or improve the odds of a risky journey or worse business deal. Dragon Child Toy Shop Madam Lian Zhu and her grandson Bo offer carved dragons, wind-up lions, puzzle boxes, painted soldiers, paper lantern kits, and tiny clockwork beasts for children and suspiciously enthusiastic adults. Nine Lantern Import Hall Silk, porcelain, spices, paper charms, enchanted fans, rare teas, medicinal roots, and questionable “authentic relics.” Red Wheel Cartwright Demonstration Yard Lu Han, better known as “Cullen Bowhandle,” offers chariots, wagons, wheels, harnesses, axle repair, and a live demonstration of “proper load balance.” Fewer idiots loading it are not covered by warranty. Food Worth Missing a Train For ¶ Brochure What It Promises Borb’s Buns — Hot Steam, Full Hearts Borb and Marda Bunbury serve bao, dumplings, meat pies, sweets, and a line full of dockhands, rail workers, market aunties, and customers who brought their own chairs. Order loudly if certain, bravely if not, and do not ask Borb for ketchup. Kardarsha’s Curds & Curios — Arena Pop-Up Everyday wheels, battle bites, enchanted wedges, cursed clearance cheese, and samples sold by a cat who believes victory must be lined with dairy. Lactose-tolerance potions available for the brave but biologically unprepared. Rainy Day Armskirk for Miserable Tourists Covered markets, tea houses, museums, bathhouses, indoor food stalls, and warm places to complain about the weather. See the Respectable City ¶ Brochure What It Promises Grand Promenade Highlights A polished walking route through Armskirk’s finest hotels, hospitals, theaters, monuments, salons, and civic plazas. The Lion & Crown Historic Hotel Tour Famous guests, private balconies, chandelier-lit halls, and old portraits that may judge you. Old Armskirk in Two Hours or Less Alleys, monuments, old bridges, civic landmarks, and “authentic” history at a pace achievable only if being chased. Museum of Heroic Misunderstandings Wax figures, battle dioramas, inaccurate plaques, and a gift shop selling tiny swords to children. Museum of Illusions & Questionable Optics Impossible staircases, talking mirrors, vanishing doors, fake ghosts, and one hallway that insists it is longer on the inside. The Grand Marionette Hall Royal scandals, tragic clowns, tiny guillotines, heroic mice, and family entertainment according to an unusually broad definition of “family.” Armskirk Clocktower Ascent Sweeping city views, bell history, civic architecture, and mild regret halfway up the stairs. Grand Library Researcher’s Pass Marble halls, spiral stacks, maps, newspapers, and assistance from Grand Librarian Horace Folio—provided your question is specific and your page corners remain unfolded. Romance, Nightlife, and Plausible Deniability ¶ Brochure What It Promises Moonlit Canal Gondolas Private rides through lantern-lit waterways with music, wine, and dramatic sighing available for an additional fee. Wetwood's Brokeback Outfitters — Get High Together! Clint Wetwood guides mountain excursions for bachelors, confirmed bachelors, and men who become confirmed somewhere above the tree line. Includes sturdy horses, matching chaps, sunset ram-watching, secluded cabins, the famous One Bedroll Discount , and family cave packages at Putty Nutty Caverns. Bareback is a personal decision; the insurance company requires saddles. The Pink Pony Inn — Where the Fur Flies Madam Maeve Mane welcomes every well-behaved identity, while Butch Glassidy serves bardcore cocktails with professionally maintained plausible deniability. Add bar snacks, suspiciously modern lute remixes, dramatic performers, and enough private booths for everyone to mind their own business. No biting without consent. The Gilded Ring Casino & Social Club Cards, dice, fine drinks, lavish rooms, and the reliable opportunity to discover which of your instincts is most expensive. Membership has privileges; losing is open to everyone. The Velvet Cage — Tonight on Stage Cabaret, acrobatics, music, elaborate stage shows, and exclusive seating for patrons who prefer their entertainment lavish and their cloakroom questions minimal. Lovers’ Lookout Picnic Basket Deal Bread, fruit, cheese, two cups, and one bottle of Regretful Red for a romantic outing above the city. Ravens not included but unavoidable. Masquerade Ball This Weekend Masks, dancing, secret admirers, plausible deniability, and a complimentary ribbon no one explains. Lust Not Included: Discreet Lodgings Guide Private rooms, nightlife, cabarets, companionship services, and “cultural experiences” with very careful wording. Emergency Date Night Rescue Package Flowers, carriage, dinner reservation, apology card, and a backup excuse written by a professional liar. Civic Business and the Trials ¶ Brochure What It Promises Official Trials Spectator Schedule Debate times, arena exhibitions, public ceremonies, approved chants, prohibited horns, and concession locations. Schedule accuracy not guaranteed after anyone says “surprise round.” Hall of Accord Exterior Tour Statues, speeches, civic history, and absolutely no access to restricted doors no matter how confidently you walk toward them. Iron Ledger Exchange — Visitor Appointments Currency exchange, letters of credit, contract escrow, appraisals, business loans, and financial advice from people who can detect arithmetic fear. Ask for Sterling Worth. Beyond the Paved Streets ¶ Brochure What It Promises Putty Nutty Caverns — A Brokeback Family Adventure Come spelunk through the soft clay corridors of Armskirk’s most family-friendly natural wonder! Follow expert guides through glittering mineral pockets, echo chambers, and natural slides to earn the coveted “I Got Putty Nutty!” completion ribbon! Souvenir helmets are available in the gift shop. Putty Nutty Caverns has absolutely no connection to the thoroughly discredited rumor that a visitor died there. The tour company won the court case, and courts are famously never wrong. Beginner’s Crystal Cave Excursion Glowing crystals, echo pools, cave moss, gentle paths, and rocks that cost extra if you lick them. Advanced Spelunking: The Probably Safe Route Rope descents, tight passages, underground rivers, and the phrase “sign here first.” The Friendly Bat Conservatory Cave bats, fruit bats, messenger bats, educational talks, and one bat the guide insists is “just large for his age.”

docs.text: Armskirk ¶ Type: Free city and current capital of the Republic of Leonia Culture: Mercantile, theatrical, civic-minded, and loudly opinionated Population: About 165,000 permanent residents; more than 200,000 during major Trials seasons Founded: Roughly 430 years ago as a fortified ferry-market and coastal trade settlement Government seat: Hall of Accord Capital term: Year 17 of Armskirk's current twenty-year term Notable district: Xiaolong, the “Little Dragon” Known for: The Trials, public debate, markets, rain, rail traffic, and professionally delivered gossip Armskirk is the current capital of Leonia, though it does not own the title. The capital rotates among Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos every twenty years. Armskirk therefore treats national government like a very long festival: profitable, prestigious, exhausting, and eventually someone else's problem. The city is a mixture of grand civic halls, rain-dark stone, busy markets, theaters, old bridges, rail yards, lantern courts, and neighborhoods built by generations of arrivals from across Suvaria. Blue-and-gold lion banners hang over the broad avenues. Beneath them, merchants sell food, newspapers shout about politics, and citizens explain—with diagrams—how they could run the republic better. The Capital at Work ¶ The Hall of Accord is both Leonia's government complex and its grandest political stage. Public debates take place in its amphitheater before the Audience, while the Barker Circle, Jugglers, Stagehands, clerks, guards, and archivists keep the republic moving in the rooms behind it. Outside lies Audience Plaza , where speeches, protests, verdicts, festival announcements, and extremely confident arguments all compete for space. Nearby, the Charter Steps are carved with famous lines from Leonia's founding documents. Politicians use them for speeches. Hecklers use them for elevation. The Lion Line Central Depot links Armskirk with the wider republic through Leonia's joint rail venture with Tinkertown. Its schedules are clear, comprehensive, and generally accurate until a passenger begins relying on them. Districts and Landmarks ¶ For practical navigation, imagine Armskirk arranged around the Grand Promenade and Hall of Accord at its civic center. The Old Harbor and oldest streets lie northwest along the coast. The Lion Line depot , freight yards, and heavy trade district spread west and southwest. Xiaolong follows the eastern and southeastern canals. The entertainment district—including the Pink Pony—sits between the Promenade and the waterfront, where respectable visitors can reach it conveniently and deny doing so afterward. Hospital Hill rises north of the Promenade, while Candlewick Row and other older working neighborhoods fill the less polished streets around the civic center. The Grand Promenade is Armskirk dressed for company: hotels, theaters, flowered balconies, luxury shops, and streets polished by rain and municipal optimism. Xiaolong , the “Little Dragon,” is one of the city's oldest and liveliest neighborhoods. Founded by merchants, sailors, craftspeople, and laborers from Mian Lung , it is full of lanterns, tea houses, bathhouses, herbalists, shrines, martial schools, workshops, and crowded markets. Locals say, “If you can't find it in Xiaolong, it probably doesn't exist.” They usually say this while trying to sell it to you. The Lantern Courts host weddings, poetry nights, civic receptions, and arguments that began as poetry nights. Lovers' Lookout offers a beautiful view over the city's roofs, bridges, and harbor lights. Couples leave ribbons and promises there; ravens provide unsolicited supervision. The Grand Library of Armskirk holds legal archives, old newspapers, maps, and librarians who consider loud conversation a form of treason. Saint Dacius Civic Hospital crowns Hospital Hill with marble steps, stained glass, skilled healers, and enough charity galas to make suffering feel briefly well-funded. The Trial Champions' Gallery displays famous competitors' weapons, costumes, and portraits. Some champions appear to have defeated perspective itself. The Old Sewer Museum explains the proud history of municipal drainage. Its gift shop sells tiny plungers, proving civilization was worth the effort. Putty Nutty Caverns , a Wetwood's Brokeback Outfitters Family Adventure just beyond the city, offers soft clay passages, glittering mineral pockets, natural slides, souvenir helmets, and the coveted “I Got Putty Nutty!” completion ribbon. It has absolutely no connection to the thoroughly discredited rumor that a visitor died there. The tour company won the court case, and courts are famously never wrong. A Few Useful Establishments ¶ These are places to visit, not complete inventories. Ask at the counter if you need something specific—and accept that the counter may ask something specific in return. Borb's Buns — Owned and operated by Borb and Marda Bunbury with the enthusiastic interference of their family. The shop is narrow, crooked, permanently steaming, and popular with workers, guards, students, and anyone willing to accept that “emotional fillings” are nonrefundable. Do not ask Borb for ketchup. Nol is not allowed near the spice shelf, which is why Nol is usually near the spice shelf. Longzi Wanwu Pu (Dragon Child Toy Shop) — Owned by Madam Lian Zhu , assisted by her grandson Bo Zhu and a fugitive clockwork cricket named Master Click-Clack . The toys are charming, mildly magical, and only occasionally better organized than the customers. Store policy: touch gently, pay honestly, and do not duel the puppets unless you intend to lose. Kardarsha's Crown Cheeses — A traveling cheese wagon run by Kardarsha the Khajiit from Moya I , an old party vehicle enjoying an unexpected second career. Kardarsha sells ordinary cheese, unusual cheese, and cheese whose legal status depends on how one defines “awake.” Iron Ledger Exchange — One of Armskirk's best-known financial houses, handling loans, letters of credit, contract escrow, appraisals, and debt restructuring under managing director Sterling Worth . Its contracts are admirably legible, extremely comprehensive, and somehow heavier than ordinary paper. The Pink Pony Inn — A bardcore tavern where spaghetti-western drama meets gay furry cabaret. Owner Madam Maeve Mane supplies calm authority, while bison-shifter bartender Butch Glassidy supplies drinks with plausible deniability. Expect lute remixes, dramatic performers, private booths, and a strict prohibition against biting without consent. Wetwood's Brokeback Outfitters — Clint Wetwood , “the Otter with No Shame,” runs guided high-country trips from Western Livery Row and takes after-hours bookings at the Pink Pony. Packages include sturdy horses, matching chaps, sunset ram-watching, secluded cabins, the One Bedroll Discount , and family spelunking at Putty Nutty Caverns. The company slogan is: “Above Ground, Underground, and Legally in the Clear.” Yunjing Lifang (Cloud Mirror Salon) — Former theater stylist Farrah Faucet provides haircuts, hot-towel shaves, braids, fur brushing, feather oiling, horn polishing, and emergency repairs after helmets. She can tell whether you need “adventure,” “apology,” or “court appearance” before you sit down. Lianhua Tangquan and Yuzheng Wenquan — Madam Yu Zhen runs Lotus Hot Springs , offering affordable public baths, scrubs, massage, laundry, and complimentary gossip under towel rules enforced more strictly than several national laws. Jade Steam Onsen offers private pools, flowering courtyards, tea service, and staff trained not to notice who entered the next room. Jade Steam closes sharply at sunset and firmly denies offering overnight lodging, spirit arbitration, or any employee with more than four arms. Choose according to budget, alibi, and how literally you take a denial. Baicao Tang (Hundred Herbs Hall) — Doctor Cassia Fen , universally called Auntie Dote , sells affordable herbal washes, combat tonics, monster oils, throwing powders, sleep teas, hangover remedies, and professional advice against drinking all of them at once. Three kettles behind her counter are labeled MEDICINE , POISON , and DEPENDS . Yuemen Lutai (Moon Gate Open-Air Theater) — Opera, comedy, shadow plays, civic satire, and heroic tragedies beneath red lanterns. Tonight's classic is The Last Lantern at Eclipse Ford : seven farewells, one sunrise, Lincohn with an axe, and no refunds for crying. Yinzhen Caiyi (Silver Needle Tailors) — Repairs, formal fittings, festival clothes, armor-friendly alterations, hidden pockets, and emergency replacement of sleeves lost to heroism, fire, or poor judgment. Jiudeng Bolihang (Nine Lantern Import Hall) — Xiaolong's broadest market for silk, porcelain, spices, paper charms, enchanted fans, medicinal roots, rare teas, and questionable “authentic relics.” If something is fake, it is at least beautifully fake. Honglun Chefang (Red Wheel Cartwrights) — A respected Xiaolong yard run by Lu Han , known around the rail yards as “Cullen Bowhandle,” with master wheelwright Axel Grease keeping the wheels round and the proprietor's speeches reasonably brief. They promise “better balance, better luck, and fewer idiots loading it,” although only the first two are covered by warranty. Many rumors begin over the second pot; the first pot is for discovering which conversation loop everyone brought in with them. docs.text: Type: Free city and current capital of the Republic of Leonia Culture: Mercantile, theatrical, civic-minded, and loudly opinionated Population: About 165,000 permanent residents; more than 200,000 during major Trials seasons Founded: Roughly 430 years ago as a fortified ferry-market and coastal trade settlement Government seat: Hall of Accord Capital term: Year 17 of Armskirk's current twenty-year term Notable district: Xiaolong, the “Little Dragon” Known for: The Trials, public debate, markets, rain, rail traffic, and professionally delivered gossip Armskirk is the current capital of Leonia, though it does not own the title. The capital rotates among Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos every twenty years. Armskirk therefore treats national government like a very long festival: profitable, prestigious, exhausting, and eventually someone else's problem. The city is a mixture of grand civic halls, rain-dark stone, busy markets, theaters, old bridges, rail yards, lantern courts, and neighborhoods built by generations of arrivals from across Suvaria. Blue-and-gold lion banners hang over the broad avenues. Beneath them, merchants sell food, newspapers shout about politics, and citizens explain—with diagrams—how they could run the republic better.

docs.text: The Hall of Accord is both Leonia's government complex and its grandest political stage. Public debates take place in its amphitheater before the Audience, while the Barker Circle, Jugglers, Stagehands, clerks, guards, and archivists keep the republic moving in the rooms behind it. Outside lies Audience Plaza , where speeches, protests, verdicts, festival announcements, and extremely confident arguments all compete for space. Nearby, the Charter Steps are carved with famous lines from Leonia's founding documents. Politicians use them for speeches. Hecklers use them for elevation. The Lion Line Central Depot links Armskirk with the wider republic through Leonia's joint rail venture with Tinkertown. Its schedules are clear, comprehensive, and generally accurate until a passenger begins relying on them.

docs.text: For practical navigation, imagine Armskirk arranged around the Grand Promenade and Hall of Accord at its civic center. The Old Harbor and oldest streets lie northwest along the coast. The Lion Line depot , freight yards, and heavy trade district spread west and southwest. Xiaolong follows the eastern and southeastern canals. The entertainment district—including the Pink Pony—sits between the Promenade and the waterfront, where respectable visitors can reach it conveniently and deny doing so afterward. Hospital Hill rises north of the Promenade, while Candlewick Row and other older working neighborhoods fill the less polished streets around the civic center. The Grand Promenade is Armskirk dressed for company: hotels, theaters, flowered balconies, luxury shops, and streets polished by rain and municipal optimism. Xiaolong , the “Little Dragon,” is one of the city's oldest and liveliest neighborhoods. Founded by merchants, sailors, craftspeople, and laborers from Mian Lung , it is full of lanterns, tea houses, bathhouses, herbalists, shrines, martial schools, workshops, and crowded markets. Locals say, “If you can't find it in Xiaolong, it probably doesn't exist.” They usually say this while trying to sell it to you. The Lantern Courts host weddings, poetry nights, civic receptions, and arguments that began as poetry nights. Lovers' Lookout offers a beautiful view over the city's roofs, bridges, and harbor lights. Couples leave ribbons and promises there; ravens provide unsolicited supervision. The Grand Library of Armskirk holds legal archives, old newspapers, maps, and librarians who consider loud conversation a form of treason. Saint Dacius Civic Hospital crowns Hospital Hill with marble steps, stained glass, skilled healers, and enough charity galas to make suffering feel briefly well-funded. The Trial Champions' Gallery displays famous competitors' weapons, costumes, and portraits. Some champions appear to have defeated perspective itself. The Old Sewer Museum explains the proud history of municipal drainage. Its gift shop sells tiny plungers, proving civilization was worth the effort. Putty Nutty Caverns , a Wetwood's Brokeback Outfitters Family Adventure just beyond the city, offers soft clay passages, glittering mineral pockets, natural slides, souvenir helmets, and the coveted “I Got Putty Nutty!” completion ribbon. It has absolutely no connection to the thoroughly discredited rumor that a visitor died there. The tour company won the court case, and courts are famously never wrong.

docs.text: These are places to visit, not complete inventories. Ask at the counter if you need something specific—and accept that the counter may ask something specific in return. Borb's Buns — Owned and operated by Borb and Marda Bunbury with the enthusiastic interference of their family. The shop is narrow, crooked, permanently steaming, and popular with workers, guards, students, and anyone willing to accept that “emotional fillings” are nonrefundable. Do not ask Borb for ketchup. Nol is not allowed near the spice shelf, which is why Nol is usually near the spice shelf. Longzi Wanwu Pu (Dragon Child Toy Shop) — Owned by Madam Lian Zhu , assisted by her grandson Bo Zhu and a fugitive clockwork cricket named Master Click-Clack . docs.text: The Snoat Sheet ¶ A Professional's Guide to Publicly Humiliating Your Future Colleagues ¶ Your Ring at a Glance ¶ Grand Ring Authority — Wilsun Fyske: Trade, industry, and the solemn belief that every public problem deserves a privately owned solution. United Assembly — A. Hamil: Competent, prepared, respectable, and capable of turning a sentence into a committee. Veiled Concord — Darkveil: Secretive populists endorsed by the Glow Cloud. All hail. Borb's Buns — Borb: Beloved food, powerful feelings, uncertain sanitation. Questions They Are Likely to Throw at You ¶ Why should Leonia trust outsiders with leadership? Who pays for your promises? What will you do when guild profit and public need collide? How will you keep Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos pulling in the same direction? Which disaster in your history should the Audience pretend not to have heard about? Across the Other Ring ¶ The Bardy Bunch sing their answers. The Wizened & Confused forget theirs. The Guild of Mild Convenience want standardized business hours. The Protagonists Ascendant all claim to be the chosen one. Watch the Redcap Resolutes . They are the only joke that is not laughing. Dirt Deep Snoat Actually Brought ¶ Grand Ring Authority — Wilsun Fyske ¶ The Valve Shortage That Somehow Lost Three Gold ¶ Deep Snoat opens a ledger labeled ABSOLUTELY ORDINARY VALVES . “Two years ago, Wilsun's companies quietly purchased nearly every spare boiler-pressure valve in Armskirk. Three weeks later, an anonymous safety report declared the city's existing valves dangerously outdated.” “Bathhouses lost hot water. Bakeries lost steam ovens. The Lion Line pumps began making a noise engineers described as financially ominous .” “Then an independent company called the People's Emergency Pressure Relief Cooperative appeared with warehouses full of approved replacement valves. Its owner was Wilsun's former foreman, whose mortgage, business loan, and left kneecap were all held by Grand Ring creditors.” “Wilsun sold him the valves, financed his purchases, charged him warehouse rent, and persuaded the city to impose an Emergency Explosion Prevention Surcharge on every sale. A different Wilsun company collected the inspection fee.” Snoat turns the ledger sideways. The accounting does not improve. “The money passed through seven companies. One owns another, which owns a third, which owns the first. After rebates, tariffs, commissions, interest, inspection fees, and something called administrative steam , the records claim Wilsun lost three gold.” “He purchased a country estate the following week.” “His accountants are still searching for the profit. One of them has begun questioning whether numbers are legally required to mean things.” Useful attack: Wilsun created a public emergency, sold the solution through a pressured proxy, financed every stage, and collected the city's response fees. If he cannot find the profit, perhaps the Audience should help by searching his estate. United Assembly — A. Hamil ¶ A Carefully Rehearsed Spontaneous Moment ¶ Hamil's famous “unscripted” interruptions have stage directions, scheduled applause, and backup interruptions in case the first interruption is itself interrupted. Snoat also has evidence that Hamil has quietly written speeches for political rivals, allowing the Assembly to prepare both sides of an argument before anyone else learns there are sides. For presentation, Snoat produces embroidered undergarments marked A. HAMIL , recovered backstage after a late policy rehearsal with a lobbyist in a griffon costume. Hamil insists the garment was a visual aid, the griffon represented infrastructure, and all applause was coincidental. Useful attack: Ask whether Hamil wants to answer the question now or wait for the cue card instructing the Audience to believe the answer was spontaneous. Veiled Concord — Darkveil ¶ The Dog Park Voting District ¶ The Dog Park , which is neither a park nor presently known to contain dogs, is registered as Ward Zero, Precinct Bark . Dogs are prohibited from entering. People are discouraged from entering. Election officials may enter only by proving they are not election officials, at which point they are no longer authorized to enter. This has not prevented excellent turnout. The precinct lists 108 registered voters , including an empty leash, three invisible angels, a municipal bench that has never been installed, and something described only as “the candidate behind you.” It returned 123 ballots in the last civic election. Officials recounted and certified 124. Most ballots supported the Veiled Concord. Three supported A LOW HUM , one contained a wet pawprint from an animal legally classified as not a dog , and one was completed on the inside of the returning officer's eyelid. Ballots arrive in black envelopes before the election, already sealed and faintly growling. Opening one voids the ballot and occasionally the opener. Poll observers must face away from the precinct and close their eyes. Their reports consistently state that nothing improper was observed, followed by several pages of frantic underlining. Campaigning inside the Dog Park is forbidden. Darkveil denies ever entering it, which is the first statement Snoat finds completely credible. The fence is not visible, not measurable, and fully electrified. This is listed as an accessibility feature. One ballot marked ALL HAIL was counted nine times after the Glow Cloud passed overhead. The election board classified this as weather. The Concord argues that existence is an unfair residency requirement imposed by traditional parties. Its Dog Park platform includes better lighting for shadows, public drinking fountains that whisper tomorrow's weather, and a strict ban on acknowledging the shapes moving between the nonexistent trees. Useful attack: Ask Darkveil whether the Dog Park endorsed the Concord—or whether the Concord merely counted everything that growled as consent. Borb's Buns — Borb Bunbury ¶ The Apron ¶ Deep Snoat opens a sealed oilskin sack. The smell arrives first: old grease, burnt onions, wet flour, and the lingering ghost of a sausage that died without closure. Borb's apron was probably white during a more innocent century. It is now layered with gravy stains, flour paste, hardened frosting, and enough rendered fat to repel light rain. Three failed inspection notices are stuck to it permanently. One pocket contains a petrified bun; another appears to be growing chives. The apron is stiff enough to stand unsupported, and when Snoat unfolds it, something inside quietly resigns and crawls away. Across the chest, beneath several geological layers of dinner, are the words: KISS THE COOK — IMMUNITY NOT INCLUDED Snoat places the apron on the table. It remains upright. “Three inspectors cited this garment. One retired. One became a priest. The third now evaluates buildings because they move less.” Useful attack: Borb's sanitation is indefensible. Unfortunately, so is making the republic's beloved bun seller look sad on live scrying crystal. Deploy the apron carefully; it may create sympathy, nausea, or lunch orders. Pocket-Sized Dirt ¶ Wilsun owns a portrait of himself signing the contract for the portrait. A smaller copy of the portrait appears inside it. Hamil's applause schedule includes a five-second allowance for “authentic public surprise.” A Veiled Concord expense report was submitted in disappearing ink and approved before anyone could read it. Borb stores inspection notices beneath a cashbox labeled NOT BUNS . The party's civic paperwork lists Moya once as transportation, once as property, and once as a dependent. All three forms were approved. Final Advice ¶ The best argument does not always win. The best moment usually does. docs.text: Deep Snoat opens a ledger labeled ABSOLUTELY ORDINARY VALVES . “Two years ago, Wilsun's companies quietly purchased nearly every spare boiler-pressure valve in Armskirk. Three weeks later, an anonymous safety report declared the city's existing valves dangerously outdated.” “Bathhouses lost hot water. Bakeries lost steam ovens. The Lion Line pumps began making a noise engineers described as financially ominous .” “Then an independent company called the People's Emergency Pressure Relief Cooperative appeared with warehouses full of approved replacement valves. Its owner was Wilsun's former foreman, whose mortgage, business loan, and left kneecap were all held by Grand Ring creditors.” “Wilsun sold him the valves, financed his purchases, charged him warehouse rent, and persuaded the city to impose an Emergency Explosion Prevention Surcharge on every sale. A different Wilsun company collected the inspection fee.” Snoat turns the ledger sideways. The accounting does not improve. “The money passed through seven companies. One owns another, which owns a third, which owns the first. After rebates, tariffs, commissions, interest, inspection fees, and something called administrative steam , the records claim Wilsun lost three gold.” “He purchased a country estate the following week.” “His accountants are still searching for the profit. One of them has begun questioning whether numbers are legally required to mean things.” Useful attack: Wilsun created a public emergency, sold the solution through a pressured proxy, financed every stage, and collected the city's response fees. docs.text: The Dog Park , which is neither a park nor presently known to contain dogs, is registered as Ward Zero, Precinct Bark . Dogs are prohibited from entering. People are discouraged from entering. Election officials may enter only by proving they are not election officials, at which point they are no longer authorized to enter. This has not prevented excellent turnout. The precinct lists 108 registered voters , including an empty leash, three invisible angels, a municipal bench that has never been installed, and something described only as “the candidate behind you.” It returned 123 ballots in the last civic election. Officials recounted and certified 124. Most ballots supported the Veiled Concord. Three supported A LOW HUM , one contained a wet pawprint from an animal legally classified as not a dog , and one was completed on the inside of the returning officer's eyelid. Ballots arrive in black envelopes before the election, already sealed and faintly growling. Opening one voids the ballot and occasionally the opener. Poll observers must face away from the precinct and close their eyes. Their reports consistently state that nothing improper was observed, followed by several pages of frantic underlining. Campaigning inside the Dog Park is forbidden. Darkveil denies ever entering it, which is the first statement Snoat finds completely credible. The fence is not visible, not measurable, and fully electrified. This is listed as an accessibility feature. One ballot marked ALL HAIL was counted nine times after the Glow Cloud passed overhead. The election board classified this as weather. The Concord argues that existence is an unfair residency requirement imposed by traditional parties. Its Dog Park platform includes better lighting for shadows, public drinking fountains that whisper tomorrow's weather, and a strict ban on acknowledging the shapes moving between the nonexistent trees. Useful attack: Ask Darkveil whether the Dog Park endorsed the Concord—or whether the Concord merely counted everything that growled as consent.

docs.text: Deep Snoat opens a sealed oilskin sack. The smell arrives first: old grease, burnt onions, wet flour, and the lingering ghost of a sausage that died without closure. Borb's apron was probably white during a more innocent century. It is now layered with gravy stains, flour paste, hardened frosting, and enough rendered fat to repel light rain. Three failed inspection notices are stuck to it permanently. One pocket contains a petrified bun; another appears to be growing chives. The apron is stiff enough to stand unsupported, and when Snoat unfolds it, something inside quietly resigns and crawls away. Across the chest, beneath several geological layers of dinner, are the words: KISS THE COOK — IMMUNITY NOT INCLUDED Snoat places the apron on the table. It remains upright. “Three inspectors cited this garment. One retired. One became a priest. The third now evaluates buildings because they move less.” Useful attack: Borb's sanitation is indefensible. Unfortunately, so is making the republic's beloved bun seller look sad on live scrying crystal. Deploy the apron carefully; it may create sympathy, nausea, or lunch orders.

All living creatures within the field have advantage on saves vs both magical and nonmagical ailments . Ongoing disease is suppressed while a creature remains in the field. docs.text: Recovered Archive Summary ¶ The Civic Contentment Bureau and the Grand Office of Civic Cheer ¶ Prepared by Grand Librarian Horace Folio from records that officially did not exist, twice. The Modern Office ¶ Name: Grand Bureau of Civic Contentment Authorized lifespan: Eleven days Payments approved: Six Programs funded: Public Morale Kitchens, Green Route Couriers, Civic Nutrition Review, Open Ring Petition Hospitality , greenhouse supplies, and emergency food wagons Approving authority: A bundled authorization bearing the Vice-Ringleader's seal Current status: Dissolved before its rented furniture arrived The seal appears authentic, but its spacing follows a government style abandoned twenty-five years ago. This suggests the seal was copied from an older document rather than applied by Vice-Ringleader Andruw Junction. The Open Ring Connection ¶ Four vendors paid by the modern Bureau also supplied free meals, temporary workers, and greenhouse freight to the campaign that pressured Leonia to pass the Open Ring Accord . Older manifests connect two of those vendors to hospitality events supporting Mycoterra's rejected provincial petition five years ago. This does not prove that every supporter or signature was false. It proves that someone repeatedly used a genuine political movement as cover for the same food, courier, and cultivation network. Frankquill circled the matching route codes and wrote: “Same soup. New office. More voters.” The Wartime Office ¶ Its seal and account codes belonged originally to the similarly named Grand Office of Civic Cheer, Nutrition, and Labor Harmony , an agency of the former Confederated Cap States of Mycoterra . The office: Distributed compulsory work rations Managed agricultural labor assignments Tracked escaped slaves Censored casualty reports Used calming mushroom cultures in its so-called One-Up Work Rations Contracted House Calhoun of Forks Hollow to conduct numbered ration trials Its surviving slogan reads: ONE PEOPLE. ONE PURPOSE. ONE-UP. A cheerful worker is a productive worker. A productive worker has nothing to fear. Frankquill's Request ¶ Shortly before his death, High Juggler Benny Frankquill requested: The original wartime charter The ration formula Modern vendors using GOC , GREEN ROUTE , or KEEP DAMP routing codes Every payment involving Mallow & Sons Import Storage He left one handwritten note: “The numbers are not merely growing roots. They are growing old roots.” Unresolved Questions ¶ Who disguised the old office's account codes beneath the Civic Contentment Bureau? docs.text: Four vendors paid by the modern Bureau also supplied free meals, temporary workers, and greenhouse freight to the campaign that pressured Leonia to pass the Open Ring Accord . docs.text: Mian Lung ¶ Type: Province of the Republic of Leonia Historic name: The Jade Kingdom Location: Eastern coast of Leonia People: The Mian Provincial leader: Chancellor Jack E. Chan Known for: Soldiers, sword saints, river trade, old traditions Mian Lung is an old eastern realm inside a young republic. Its history predates Leonia, its people retain a strong identity of their own, and its soldiers form the backbone of the republic's armed forces. The name Mian Lung is commonly translated as “Distant from the Dragon.” Mian tradition says its people are ancient wanderers from a faraway kingdom called Shou Lung , “Receiver of the Dragon.” The journey is too old to verify and too good a story to stop telling. Land and People ¶ Mian Lung stretches along Leonia's eastern coastline. River valleys, wooded foothills, fishing villages, fortified settlements, and old city-states shape the province. Xuán Ji , the “Mysterious River,” is among its best-known regions. For generations, the noble Fang family supervised trade along its river and foothills. The Mian have a reputation for discipline, duty, skilled craftsmanship, and formidable martial traditions. Fishing, trapping, river trade, farming, forestry, and military service have all shaped life here. Urban expansion has also consumed forests and other natural resources, driving old nature spirits deeper into the wilds. Mian Lung has excellent roads to history and several potholes to modernity. Deuce Leem, Guardian of Xuán Ji ¶ Deuce Leem is a powerful water spirit traditionally said to guard the Xuán Ji. He seldom leaves the river, preferring to answer problems by flowing around them, through them, or—when the problem is an invading army—directly over them. During the War of Broken Chains, trapped Mian soldiers beat the old water drums and called for aid at Eclipse Ford. Deuce answered from Xuán Ji and strengthened the failing sluice flood that broke the New Moon Battalion. Lincohn handled the vampire officers; Deuce handled the water; generations of playwrights have handled the credit. Mian martial artists often repeat his best-known advice: “Be water, my friend.” Shrines depict him in dozens of contradictory fighting stances, but all agree that his hair looked excellent in the rain. Current Crisis: The Fires in Mian Lung ¶ Mian Lung is burning again. A new order called the Jǐn Bào , or “Golden Leopards,” claims it will restore balance through fire. Its leader, Master Zhaoyan , preaches purity and obedience to the flame. The results are less poetic than the speeches. Villages have vanished, temples have fallen silent, and the Mógu Chóng Bài have gone into hiding. Refugees describe rivers black with ash and feline shadows moving across rooftops at dawn. Fang Ro received a scroll sealed in red wax and bearing her name in Infernal. She recognizes the Jǐn Bào's rhetoric from earlier violence and believed she had already ended whatever movement inspired it. Fang has left the party and returned to Mian Lung to aid her homeland; Black Chao has joined the party in her absence. What the Jǐn Bào truly wants, whether the reports of feline shadows are literal, and who sent Fang's infernal message remain unknown. Mian Lung currently has more questions than answers and significantly more fire than either. From Jade Kingdom to Leonian Province ¶ About two hundred years ago, an earthquake in the Qlohsh Highlands unleashed an infernal army. A breakaway force marched east, destroyed settlements, and threatened Mian Lung before warnings could reach the province. Mian Lung fought that incursion as the independent Jade Kingdom. During the same broad era of regional danger, Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos formed their own mutual-protection pact. Their alliance became the Republic of Leonia; Mian Lung was not one of its founding members. After Leonia existed, the Jade Kingdom signed a separate mutual-defense treaty with the new republic. The two states cooperated against common threats, but Mian Lung remained sovereign. About one hundred years ago, the Jade-Lion Concord made Mian Lung a full province of Leonia. The agreement preserved the office of Chancellor and many local institutions while formalizing military service, taxes, food levies, and Mian representation in national government. Leonian historians call this “full inclusion.” Mian historians often call it “the second agreement, with considerably more fine print.” Government and Leonia ¶ Mian Lung is governed locally by Chancellor Jack E. Chan , who also represents the province before the Ringleader's government. The province retains older laws, customs, titles, and institutions so long as they do not conflict with the Leonian charter. Mian Lung pays substantial tax and food levies to the republic and supplies a large share of its professional soldiers. The Mian have honored those obligations for generations, though “honored” and “enjoyed” are very different verbs. The Nine Tables and One Ballot ¶ Mian Lung elects its Chancellor every six years through the Nine Tables and One Ballot . Prospective candidates must first earn endorsements from nine traditional constituencies: farmers, fishers, soldiers, artisans, merchants, scholars, temples, city wards, and rural clans. They then face a day-long public examination conducted at nine literal tables. The tests include interpreting law, balancing a granary ledger, settling a mock boundary dispute, planning a flood evacuation, and brewing tea while elderly spectators loudly explain how the previous candidate did it better. Anyone who survives all nine tables without fleeing, bribing an examiner, or declaring war on the audience earns a place on the ballot. The province then chooses its Chancellor by ranked-choice vote. This preserves the ancient principle that leaders should possess wisdom, patience, practical skill, and at least one afternoon they will never discuss again. The victor is inaugurated beneath an enormous golden dragon puppet carried by eighty volunteers. Tradition requires the dragon to bow before the new Chancellor. Tradition also forbids enlarging the palace doors, so the inauguration has taken place outside for 312 consecutive years. The Chancellor administers Mian Lung's provincial budget, granaries, roads, canals, civil defense, local courts, and civil appointments. The office may mobilize provincial forces during an immediate emergency, but sustained national deployment belongs to Leonia's Master of the Muster. At the Hall of Accord, the Chancellor occupies the separate Jade Seat rather than joining the six-member Barker Circle. The Jade Seat has a binding vote on changes to the Jade-Lion Concord, Mian taxes and food levies, deployment of Mian forces beyond the province, and national laws written specifically for Mian Lung. On other national business, the Chancellor may speak, advise, object, and produce an intimidating quantity of documentation, but does not cast a Barker vote. Chancellor Jack E. Chan ¶ Jack E. Chan is a former civil-defense organizer and treaty negotiator who would rather fix a problem himself than order someone else into danger. He is warm, practical, self-deprecating, and remarkably capable, though rarely dignified while demonstrating it. He has been known to catch falling scrolls, teacups, and pieces of furniture without interrupting a meeting. When violence is unavoidable, he favors improvised objects, rapid movement, and apologizing to whatever he breaks. He has an ancient and deeply personal feud with ladders. Chan supports the republic but argues that Leonia too often treats Mian Lung as a barracks and pantry rather than a full province. He wants fairer levies, greater provincial investment, and recognition for what the Mian contribute beyond military service. His greatest weakness is that he delegates poorly. Chan will exhaust himself protecting others long after a wiser leader would have asked for help. “Government is like a ladder: useful, necessary, and always falling toward the person least prepared to catch it.” The Martial State ¶ Military service is central to Mian Lung's public identity. In ordinary times, its forces range from local levies and trained infantry to cavalry, shi knights, and elite companies. During major incursions, conscription may be imposed. The most celebrated elite warriors are the jiàn shèng , or “sword saints.” They train from youth with the jiàn and horn bow, combining discipline, mobility, and an alarming ability to turn “unarmored” into a threat. The Night Tigers are an elite Mian company commanded by Heise Chao Ping , better known as Black Chao . The company earned its reputation surviving infernal attacks and later developed difficult war games designed to remove the undeserving, the soft, and anyone who thought training was going unusually well. The Fang and the Bái Láng ¶ The Fang of Xuán Ji were ennobled before Leonia existed. Their patriarch traditionally bore the title Gong , or Duke. During the first great infernal incursion, the Fang lands were overwhelmed until the neighboring Bái Láng , or “White Wolves,” came to their aid. The Bái Láng are yaoguài : natural shapeshifters with human, animal, and hybrid forms. They are not lycanthropes, do not spread their nature through bites, and are no more beholden to the moon than an ordinary wolf. Fang and Bái Láng families later intermarried, producing bloodlines touched by shapeshifting magic. That union was once considered holy. As Mian society became more urban and distant from the old spirits, mixed-blood Fang fell in social standing and were often treated as wild, unreliable, or “impure.” Many moved away from major settlements and worked as hunters, trappers, fishers, and farmers. The prejudice remains part of Mian Lung's history—and, in some places, its present. Faith and the Deep Places ¶ Beneath the foothills of Xuán Ji lie caves and hidden temples associated with the Mógu Chóng Bài , the “Cult of the Fungus.” Its spore druids protect underground places and preserve traditions overlooked by the growing city-states. The Mógu are neither a single cheerful mushroom club nor a single sinister cult. Like most religious communities, they include teachers, guardians, mystics, zealots, and at least one person who has made the meeting unnecessarily complicated. Fang Ro and Black Chao ¶ Fang Ro , also called Seiqua , was born in Xuán Ji to Tengfei and Lian. Descended from both Fang and Bái Láng bloodlines, she learned wilderness skills from her fisherman and trapper father, trained with the Mógu Chóng Bài, and later became a jiàn shèng in the Mian army. An infernal attack led by Ulysses Vex destroyed her village and killed her family. Fang Ro survived, but Vex severed her tongue with the hell-forged blade Gloomfire. Her pursuit of Vex eventually carried her away from Mian Lung and into the party's adventures. Black Chao is a Mian infantry leader and commander of the Night Tigers. He lost his left eye during the same campaign and survived to rebuild the company around its remaining veterans. Chao considers Fang Ro a little sister and sometimes calls her Heise Ro , or “Black Ro,” as a sign of kinship—even when disagreeing loudly with nearly every decision she makes. General Wei Shen , currently Leonia's Master of the Muster, is also Mian-born and remains deeply respected among the province's soldiers and veterans. Mian Lung Beyond the Province ¶ Generations of Mian merchants, sailors, artisans, soldiers, and laborers have settled elsewhere in Leonia. Their most visible community is Xiaolong , the “Little Dragon” district of Armskirk . Xiaolong's lantern festivals, tea houses, martial schools, bathhouses, herbalists, shrines, import halls, and food stalls make it a cultural bridge between Mian Lung and the Free Cities. Residents often consider themselves fully Leonian and proudly Mian, demonstrating that identity can do two things at once even when government paperwork cannot.

docs.text: Deuce Leem is a powerful water spirit traditionally said to guard the Xuán Ji. He seldom leaves the river, preferring to answer problems by flowing around them, through them, or—when the problem is an invading army—directly over them. During the War of Broken Chains, trapped Mian soldiers beat the old water drums and called for aid at Eclipse Ford. Deuce answered from Xuán Ji and strengthened the failing sluice flood that broke the New Moon Battalion. Lincohn handled the vampire officers; Deuce handled the water; generations of playwrights have handled the credit. Mian martial artists often repeat his best-known advice: “Be water, my friend.” Shrines depict him in dozens of contradictory fighting stances, but all agree that his hair looked excellent in the rain.
docs.title: Deuce Leem, Guardian of Xuán Ji

docs.text: Mian Lung is burning again. A new order called the Jǐn Bào , or “Golden Leopards,” claims it will restore balance through fire. Its leader, Master Zhaoyan , preaches purity and obedience to the flame. The results are less poetic than the speeches. Villages have vanished, temples have fallen silent, and the Mógu Chóng Bài have gone into hiding. Refugees describe rivers black with ash and feline shadows moving across rooftops at dawn. Fang Ro received a scroll sealed in red wax and bearing her name in Infernal. She recognizes the Jǐn Bào's rhetoric from earlier violence and believed she had already ended whatever movement inspired it. Fang has left the party and returned to Mian Lung to aid her homeland; Black Chao has joined the party in her absence. What the Jǐn Bào truly wants, whether the reports of feline shadows are literal, and who sent Fang's infernal message remain unknown. Mian Lung currently has more questions than answers and significantly more fire than either.
docs.title: Current Crisis: The Fires in Mian Lung

docs.text: About two hundred years ago, an earthquake in the Qlohsh Highlands unleashed an infernal army. A breakaway force marched east, destroyed settlements, and threatened Mian Lung before warnings could reach the province. Mian Lung fought that incursion as the independent Jade Kingdom. During the same broad era of regional danger, Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos formed their own mutual-protection pact. Their alliance became the Republic of Leonia; Mian Lung was not one of its founding members. After Leonia existed, the Jade Kingdom signed a separate mutual-defense treaty with the new republic. The two states cooperated against common threats, but Mian Lung remained sovereign. About one hundred years ago, the Jade-Lion Concord made Mian Lung a full province of Leonia. The agreement preserved the office of Chancellor and many local institutions while formalizing military service, taxes, food levies, and Mian representation in national government. Leonian historians call this “full inclusion.” Mian historians often call it “the second agreement, with considerably more fine print.”
docs.title: From Jade Kingdom to Leonian Province

docs.text: Mian Lung is governed locally by Chancellor Jack E. Chan , who also represents the province before the Ringleader's government. The province retains older laws, customs, titles, and institutions so long as they do not conflict with the Leonian charter. Mian Lung pays substantial tax and food levies to the republic and supplies a large share of its professional soldiers. The Mian have honored those obligations for generations, though “honored” and “enjoyed” are very different verbs.
docs.title: Government and Leonia

docs.text: Mian Lung elects its Chancellor every six years through the Nine Tables and One Ballot . Prospective candidates must first earn endorsements from nine traditional constituencies: farmers, fishers, soldiers, artisans, merchants, scholars, temples, city wards, and rural clans. They then face a day-long public examination conducted at nine literal tables. The tests include interpreting law, balancing a granary ledger, settling a mock boundary dispute, planning a flood evacuation, and brewing tea while elderly spectators loudly explain how the previous candidate did it better. Anyone who survives all nine tables without fleeing, bribing an examiner, or declaring war on the audience earns a place on the ballot. The province then chooses its Chancellor by ranked-choice vote. This preserves the ancient principle that leaders should possess wisdom, patience, practical skill, and at least one afternoon they will never discuss again. The victor is inaugurated beneath an enormous golden dragon puppet carried by eighty volunteers. Tradition requires the dragon to bow before the new Chancellor. Tradition also forbids enlarging the palace doors, so the inauguration has taken place outside for 312 consecutive years. The Chancellor administers Mian Lung's provincial budget, granaries, roads, canals, civil defense, local courts, and civil appointments. The office may mobilize provincial forces during an immediate emergency, but sustained national deployment belongs to Leonia's Master of the Muster. At the Hall of Accord, the Chancellor occupies the separate Jade Seat rather than joining the six-member Barker Circle. The Jade Seat has a binding vote on changes to the Jade-Lion Concord, Mian taxes and food levies, deployment of Mian forces beyond the province, and national laws written specifically for Mian Lung. On other national business, the Chancellor may speak, advise, object, and produce an intimidating quantity of documentation, but does not cast a Barker vote.
docs.title: The Nine Tables and One Ballot

docs.text: Jack E. Chan is a former civil-defense organizer and treaty negotiator who would rather fix a problem himself than order someone else into danger. He is warm, practical, self-deprecating, and remarkably capable, though rarely dignified while demonstrating it. He has been known to catch falling scrolls, teacups, and pieces of furniture without interrupting a meeting. When violence is unavoidable, he favors improvised objects, rapid movement, and apologizing to whatever he breaks. He has an ancient and deeply personal feud with ladders. Chan supports the republic but argues that Leonia too often treats Mian Lung as a barracks and pantry rather than a full province. He wants fairer levies, greater provincial investment, and recognition for what the Mian contribute beyond military service. His greatest weakness is that he delegates poorly. Chan will exhaust himself protecting others long after a wiser leader would have asked for help. “Government is like a ladder: useful, necessary, and always falling toward the person least prepared to catch it.”
docs.title: Chancellor Jack E. Chan

docs.text: Military service is central to Mian Lung's public identity. In ordinary times, its forces range from local levies and trained infantry to cavalry, shi knights, and elite companies. During major incursions, conscription may be imposed. The most celebrated elite warriors are the jiàn shèng , or “sword saints.” They train from youth with the jiàn and horn bow, combining discipline, mobility, and an alarming ability to turn “unarmored” into a threat. The Night Tigers are an elite Mian company commanded by Heise Chao Ping , better known as Black Chao . The company earned its reputation surviving infernal attacks and later developed difficult war games designed to remove the undeserving, the soft, and anyone who thought training was going unusually well.
docs.title: The Martial State

docs.text: The Fang of Xuán Ji were ennobled before Leonia existed. Their patriarch traditionally bore the title Gong , or Duke. During the first great infernal incursion, the Fang lands were overwhelmed until the neighboring Bái Láng , or “White Wolves,” came to their aid. The Bái Láng are yaoguài : natural shapeshifters with human, animal, and hybrid forms. They are not lycanthropes, do not spread their nature through bites, and are no more beholden to the moon than an ordinary wolf. Fang and Bái Láng families later intermarried, producing bloodlines touched by shapeshifting magic. That union was once considered holy. As Mian society became more urban and distant from the old spirits, mixed-blood Fang fell in social standing and were often treated as wild, unreliable, or “impure.” Many moved away from major settlements and worked as hunters, trappers, fishers, and farmers. The prejudice remains part of Mian Lung's history—and, in some places, its present.
docs.title: The Fang and the Bái Láng

docs.text: Beneath the foothills of Xuán Ji lie caves and hidden temples associated with the Mógu Chóng Bài , the “Cult of the Fungus.” Its spore druids protect underground places and preserve traditions overlooked by the growing city-states. The Mógu are neither a single cheerful mushroom club nor a single sinister cult. Like most religious communities, they include teachers, guardians, mystics, zealots, and at least one person who has made the meeting unnecessarily complicated.
docs.title: Faith and the Deep Places

docs.text: Fang Ro , also called Seiqua , was born in Xuán Ji to Tengfei and Lian. Descended from both Fang and Bái Láng bloodlines, she learned wilderness skills from her fisherman and trapper father, trained with the Mógu Chóng Bài, and later became a jiàn shèng in the Mian army. An infernal attack led by Ulysses Vex destroyed her village and killed her family. Fang Ro survived, but Vex severed her tongue with the hell-forged blade Gloomfire. Her pursuit of Vex eventually carried her away from Mian Lung and into the party's adventures. Black Chao is a Mian infantry leader and commander of the Night Tigers. He lost his left eye during the same campaign and survived to rebuild the company around its remaining veterans. Chao considers Fang Ro a little sister and sometimes calls her Heise Ro , or “Black Ro,” as a sign of kinship—even when disagreeing loudly with nearly every decision she makes. General Wei Shen , currently Leonia's Master of the Muster, is also Mian-born and remains deeply respected among the province's soldiers and veterans.
docs.title: Fang Ro and Black Chao

docs.text: Generations of Mian merchants, sailors, artisans, soldiers, and laborers have settled elsewhere in Leonia. Their most visible community is Xiaolong , the “Little Dragon” district of Armskirk . Xiaolong's lantern festivals, tea houses, martial schools, bathhouses, herbalists, shrines, import halls, and food stalls make it a cultural bridge between Mian Lung and the Free Cities. Residents often consider themselves fully Leonian and proudly Mian, demonstrating that identity can do two things at once even when government paperwork cannot.
docs.title: Mian Lung Beyond the Province

docs.text: Republic of Leonia ¶ Type: Nation Government: Federal democracy Founding cities: Armskirk , Torath, and Corvos Province: Mian Lung Current capital: Armskirk Head of government: Ringleader Lincohn Abraham National symbol: The lion The Republic of Leonia lies in the far east of Suvaria. It is the youngest nation on the continent, although Leonian officials have already produced enough speeches, statues, and commemorative mugs to make it feel much older. Leonia did not exist before the alliance of Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos. About two centuries ago, the three sovereign free cities created a mutual-protection pact. That alliance gradually grew into shared laws, trade agreements, public institutions, and—after what historians politely call several energetic disagreements —the federal Republic of Leonia. The founding cities were fiercely independent and had no interest in trading three local rulers for one distant monarch. The republic was therefore built to preserve local identity while giving the cities a common defense and national government. Leonian politics has been arguing over where local freedom ends and federal authority begins ever since. Most citizens consider the arguing an essential public service. The Three Free Cities and Mian Lung ¶ Each city keeps its own customs and civic identity while participating in the government of the republic. Armskirk sits on the northwestern coast of Leonia's eastern peninsula. It is the current capital: a rain-polished city of government halls, markets, theaters, rail traffic, and confident public opinions. Torath is a mountain city of rail yards, arenas, performance halls, strong cheese, and the serene conviction that everyone else is pronouncing it wrong. Corvos is a coastal city of shipyards, lighthouses, aqueducts, and patient negotiators who consider silence a complete counteroffer. Mian Lung is an older eastern realm that remained separate when Leonia was founded. It later entered a mutual-defense treaty with the republic and became a full province roughly one hundred years ago while retaining a Chancellor and many local institutions. The national capital rotates among the three founding cities every twenty years. Mian Lung participates in the republic but is not part of the capital rotation. Armskirk currently has the privilege, responsibility, and municipal headache of hosting it. Government ¶ Leonian politics borrows its titles from the circus. This is not because government is a joke. It is because Leonians believe power should perform in public, face the crowd, and occasionally be pelted with fruit. The Ringleader is the republic's elected head of government. A Ringleader serves one five-year term and cannot immediately stand for another. The Barker Circle is the executive council. Its members administer the republic and explain its decisions to the public—sometimes in that order. The Jugglers oversee taxes, tariffs, budgets, and trade. They insist the name refers to balancing competing needs, not making public money disappear. The Stagehands oversee roads, rail, civic construction, and other public works. When everything functions, nobody sees them. When it does not, everybody suddenly becomes an engineer. The Audience is the citizen body from which the government draws its legitimacy. Citizens vote, petition, attend debates, cheer, heckle, and maintain the sacred democratic right to complain about the results. The Hall of Accord in Armskirk currently houses the national government. Its public chambers resemble an amphitheater more than a throne room: circular stages, packed galleries, speaking horns, banners, and enough acoustics to make a minor procedural objection sound like a declaration of war. Current Leadership ¶ Office Holder Public responsibility Ringleader Lincohn Abraham Head of government and defender of the republic's charter Vice-Ringleader Andruw Junction Administration, logistics, and coordination among the cities Master of the Muster General Wei Shen Defense, militias, emergency response, and Trials security Keeper of the Charter Magister Pica Draft Laws, records, archives, and official decrees Voice of the Republic Dolly Mannerly Ceremonies, public announcements, and civic messaging High Juggler Benny Frankquill Taxes, tariffs, budgets, treasury, and trade policy Chancellor of Mian Lung Jack E. Chan Provincial government and Mian representation before the Ringleader The Chancellor occupies Mian Lung's separate Jade Seat , not a seventh place in the Barker Circle. The seat carries a binding vote when national decisions alter the province's levies, military deployments, treaty rights, or the Jade-Lion Concord; otherwise the Chancellor advises the government with all the authority of a very old treaty and an extremely heavy binder. Ringleader Abraham has reached his term limit and is stepping down rather than seeking a way around it. In Leonia, voluntarily leaving office is considered either the highest form of civic virtue or proof that someone has finally read all the paperwork. The Trials of the Three Cities ¶ Every five years, Leonia chooses its next Ringleader through the Trials of the Three Cities . The Trials combine ritual competition, public spectacle, political campaigning, and civic judgment. Teams put forward a candidate for Ringleader and compete before the Audience. The exact sequence, scoring, and oldest rites are intentionally secretive. Some challenges test strength or skill; others test judgment, persuasion, teamwork, or the ability to remain dignified while the entire republic watches. Officials reveal rules when tradition requires it, which is a ceremonial way of saying at the last possible moment . The current Trials opened in Armskirk with a spectacular Super Clash Bros competition. The surviving teams now advance toward a public debate. Beyond that, contestants receive the same reassuring guidance given to generations before them: prepare for anything, trust the judges, and sign the waiver. The War of Broken Chains ¶ Twenty-five years ago, neighboring Mycoterra was still the Confederated Cap States : thirteen slaveholding states ruled from Richmire by vampire aristocrats. Their laws called slavery Royal Bond Service and sold feeding rights alongside labor contracts. This improved neither the slavery nor the vampires, although it produced considerably more paperwork. Enslaved Mycoterrans and abolitionists built their own liberation movement. Harriet Tubers guided families through the Underground Pipeway , Frederick Sporeglass rallied the country through speeches and newspapers, Ulysses S. Grantoad commanded the Army of the Free Caps, and William Tecumseh Shrooman broke Confederate supply lines during the March to the Green Sea. Young Leonian Lincohn Abraham joined the rebellion as a vampire hunter, wielding his silver-edged axe The Railsplitter against officers who treated death as a brief scheduling conflict. Mian Lung 's Jade Lantern Relief Company carried healers and engineers into the war, and its soldiers' water drums famously summoned Deuce Leem , guardian of Xuán Ji, at Eclipse Ford. The fighting passed through Fort Shroomter, Gettyspore, the Thwomp Trenches, and Eclipse Ford before Operation Breaking Dawn brought down Richmire and Blood Regent Toadstool. The new government abolished slavery, established citizenship, protected voting rights, and rebuilt the country as the Sporeign Dominion of Mycoterra . Mycoterrans remain quick to remind foreign admirers that they liberated themselves; Lincohn helped with the unusually persistent vampires. Mycoterra and the Open Ring ¶ The neighboring Sporeign Dominion of Mycoterra spent twenty years rebuilding after overthrowing the slaveholding vampire government that once ruled it. Five years ago, Mycoterra petitioned to become another Leonian province. Ringleader Abraham vetoed admission under the charter's Free Assent Clause after auditors found suspiciously uniform votes, matching council resolutions, and communities that inspectors could not interview privately. Critics call the veto an old soldier's prejudice; supporters call unanimous politics a contradiction wearing a very cheerful hat. This year's Open Ring Accord is the compromise. Mycoterra may sponsor the Redcap Resolutes for one Trials cycle, led by Marshal Marioni—a Mycoterran reformer who earned Leonian citizenship while rebuilding the Corvos floodworks. If Marioni wins, he may become Ringleader, but Mycoterra must still face a separate admission vote. Leonia has therefore addressed a major foreign-policy dispute in its traditional manner: public arguments, elaborate rules, and controlled property damage. Mian Lung and the Eastern Connection ¶ Mian Lung is Fang Ro's homeland, an eastern coastal province whose history predates the republic. Its merchants, craftspeople, immigrants, and soldiers have shaped Leonia for generations. Mian soldiers form the backbone of Leonian armed forces, while trade and migration have made their traditions part of daily life in the Free Cities. Armskirk's Xiaolong District , or “Little Dragon,” is the most visible expression of that relationship. Founded generations ago by people from Mian Lung, it remains a center for lantern festivals, tea houses, martial schools, bathhouses, artisans, imported goods, and food worth missing a train for. Fang Ro served among Mian Lung's warriors before traveling with the party. General Wei Shen and Black Chao also hail from Mian Lung, and their reputations carry considerable weight among soldiers and veterans in Leonia. Mian Lung is presently facing a wave of fires and disappearances blamed on the Jǐn Bào , or “Golden Leopards,” whose leader Master Zhaoyan preaches purity through flame. docs.text: Type: Nation Government: Federal democracy Founding cities: Armskirk , Torath, and Corvos Province: Mian Lung Current capital: Armskirk Head of government: Ringleader Lincohn Abraham National symbol: The lion The Republic of Leonia lies in the far east of Suvaria. It is the youngest nation on the continent, although Leonian officials have already produced enough speeches, statues, and commemorative mugs to make it feel much older. Leonia did not exist before the alliance of Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos. About two centuries ago, the three sovereign free cities created a mutual-protection pact. That alliance gradually grew into shared laws, trade agreements, public institutions, and—after what historians politely call several energetic disagreements —the federal Republic of Leonia. The founding cities were fiercely independent and had no interest in trading three local rulers for one distant monarch. The republic was therefore built to preserve local identity while giving the cities a common defense and national government. Leonian politics has been arguing over where local freedom ends and federal authority begins ever since. Most citizens consider the arguing an essential public service.
docs.title: Republic of Leonia

docs.text: Each city keeps its own customs and civic identity while participating in the government of the republic. Armskirk sits on the northwestern coast of Leonia's eastern peninsula. It is the current capital: a rain-polished city of government halls, markets, theaters, rail traffic, and confident public opinions. Torath is a mountain city of rail yards, arenas, performance halls, strong cheese, and the serene conviction that everyone else is pronouncing it wrong. Corvos is a coastal city of shipyards, lighthouses, aqueducts, and patient negotiators who consider silence a complete counteroffer. Mian Lung is an older eastern realm that remained separate when Leonia was founded. It later entered a mutual-defense treaty with the republic and became a full province roughly one hundred years ago while retaining a Chancellor and many local institutions. The national capital rotates among the three founding cities every twenty years. Mian Lung participates in the republic but is not part of the capital rotation. Armskirk currently has the privilege, responsibility, and municipal headache of hosting it.
docs.title: The Three Free Cities and Mian Lung

docs.text: Leonian politics borrows its titles from the circus. This is not because government is a joke. It is because Leonians believe power should perform in public, face the crowd, and occasionally be pelted with fruit. The Ringleader is the republic's elected head of government. A Ringleader serves one five-year term and cannot immediately stand for another. The Barker Circle is the executive council. Its members administer the republic and explain its decisions to the public—sometimes in that order. The Jugglers oversee taxes, tariffs, budgets, and trade. They insist the name refers to balancing competing needs, not making public money disappear. The Stagehands oversee roads, rail, civic construction, and other public works. When everything functions, nobody sees them. When it does not, everybody suddenly becomes an engineer. The Audience is the citizen body from which the government draws its legitimacy. Citizens vote, petition, attend debates, cheer, heckle, and maintain the sacred democratic right to complain about the results. The Hall of Accord in Armskirk currently houses the national government. Its public chambers resemble an amphitheater more than a throne room: circular stages, packed galleries, speaking horns, banners, and enough acoustics to make a minor procedural objection sound like a declaration of war.

Ringleader Abraham has reached his term limit and is stepping down rather than seeking a way around it. In Leonia, voluntarily leaving office is considered either the highest form of civic virtue or proof that someone has finally read all the paperwork.
