docs.text: Every five years, Leonia chooses its next Ringleader through the Trials of the Three Cities . The Trials combine ritual competition, public spectacle, political campaigning, and civic judgment. Teams put forward a candidate for Ringleader and compete before the Audience. The exact sequence, scoring, and oldest rites are intentionally secretive. Some challenges test strength or skill; others test judgment, persuasion, teamwork, or the ability to remain dignified while the entire republic watches. Officials reveal rules when tradition requires it, which is a ceremonial way of saying at the last possible moment . The current Trials opened in Armskirk with a spectacular Super Clash Bros competition. The surviving teams now advance toward a public debate. Beyond that, contestants receive the same reassuring guidance given to generations before them: prepare for anything, trust the judges, and sign the waiver.
docs.title: The Trials of the Three Cities

docs.text: Twenty-five years ago, neighboring Mycoterra was still the Confederated Cap States : thirteen slaveholding states ruled from Richmire by vampire aristocrats. Their laws called slavery Royal Bond Service and sold feeding rights alongside labor contracts. This improved neither the slavery nor the vampires, although it produced considerably more paperwork. Enslaved Mycoterrans and abolitionists built their own liberation movement. Harriet Tubers guided families through the Underground Pipeway , Frederick Sporeglass rallied the country through speeches and newspapers, Ulysses S. Grantoad commanded the Army of the Free Caps, and William Tecumseh Shrooman broke Confederate supply lines during the March to the Green Sea. Young Leonian Lincohn Abraham joined the rebellion as a vampire hunter, wielding his silver-edged axe The Railsplitter against officers who treated death as a brief scheduling conflict. Mian Lung 's Jade Lantern Relief Company carried healers and engineers into the war, and its soldiers' water drums famously summoned Deuce Leem , guardian of Xuán Ji, at Eclipse Ford. The fighting passed through Fort Shroomter, Gettyspore, the Thwomp Trenches, and Eclipse Ford before Operation Breaking Dawn brought down Richmire and Blood Regent Toadstool. The new government abolished slavery, established citizenship, protected voting rights, and rebuilt the country as the Sporeign Dominion of Mycoterra . Mycoterrans remain quick to remind foreign admirers that they liberated themselves; Lincohn helped with the unusually persistent vampires.
docs.title: The War of Broken Chains

docs.text: The neighboring Sporeign Dominion of Mycoterra spent twenty years rebuilding after overthrowing the slaveholding vampire government that once ruled it. Five years ago, Mycoterra petitioned to become another Leonian province. Ringleader Abraham vetoed admission under the charter's Free Assent Clause after auditors found suspiciously uniform votes, matching council resolutions, and communities that inspectors could not interview privately. Critics call the veto an old soldier's prejudice; supporters call unanimous politics a contradiction wearing a very cheerful hat. This year's Open Ring Accord is the compromise. Mycoterra may sponsor the Redcap Resolutes for one Trials cycle, led by Marshal Marioni—a Mycoterran reformer who earned Leonian citizenship while rebuilding the Corvos floodworks. If Marioni wins, he may become Ringleader, but Mycoterra must still face a separate admission vote. Leonia has therefore addressed a major foreign-policy dispute in its traditional manner: public arguments, elaborate rules, and controlled property damage.

docs.text: Subject: 🧭 The Seek Allies Arc Begins – Four Roads, One Destiny Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Greetings, Adventurers! Tinkertown breathes again, but the world beyond its steam-belching rails is far from still. The Eternal Engine is turning—but it won’t turn the tide alone. The Council of Chaos —an ancient pact of Suvaria’s darkest powers—has begun to stir. Whether they see you as a threat… or a pawn… remains unclear. But the ground beneath your boots is shifting. It’s time to Seek Allies. Near the start of the next session, you’ll choose your destination. Each path opens new possibilities—and carries its own risks. 🧁 1. King Curry’s Hidden Truths ¶ Aunt Jill Cookie , and the women and children of King Curry’s warren, were taken to a forced labor camp in the Yundabad Mountains , near the orc city of Cheddud Bha . Curry knows where—but not what’s being built. “It hums like thunder and eats the sky.” To reach it, you’ll cross lands where Sauron’s name is law , and shadows walk in daylight. Crude maps and escape routes scratched on old parchment Rumors of a fortress so large it blots out the sun A single warning: “Not even the shadows come back from that place.” 🧙‍♀️ 2. Invitation to Hügsnorts ¶ A bat-winged cat wearing a monocle delivers a glittering letter: “You are hereby invited to tea, tutelage, and perhaps a touch of destiny.” The School of Hexcraft & Hubbub has summoned Amaryllis . The drifting city of Brithombar hides behind layers of illusion—neutral in every war, or so they claim. But something hums beneath the stillness… like magic waiting to snap. The invitation won’t stop twitching A note on the back: “Don’t trust the headmaster’s reflection.” A chance to learn what others are preparing for—or hiding from 🔥 3. Fires in Ming Lung ¶ Fang Ro’s homeland burns again. A new order—the Jǐn Bào , or “Golden Leopards” —claims to bring balance through flame. Their leader, Master Zhaoyan , preaches purity and obedience to the fire. Villages vanish. Temples fall silent. The Mógu Chóng Bài have gone into hiding. But Fang has heard this rhetoric before—beneath screams and smoke. She ended it once… or thought she did. A scroll sealed in red wax bears Fang’s name in Infernal Refugees speak of feline shadows prowling rooftops at dawn The rivers of Mian Lung now run black with ash 🏯 4. The Trials of the Three Cities ¶ Every five years, the Republic of Leonia in the far east holds a ritual competition to choose the next Ringleader . That time has come. But something feels different this year. Relics stir beneath the arenas. Prophecies resurface. And some whisper the Council’s influence has already reached the Free Cities. The competition is being held in Armskirk this time. An old ally, Kardarsha the Kajiit , can get you inside the trials One challenge is called “The Walk Between Flames” —no one agrees what it means The winner shapes the cities’ future. The losers may not leave at all 🧭 Choose Your Path ¶ Each road could earn you allies—or make new enemies. The Council of Chaos is no longer watching from afar. They are moving. So must you. See you at the table, — Your DM Blake

docs.text: Signet of the Fallen Nine ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Wondrous item (ring), very rare (requires attunement by a non-good spellcaster; cursed) Provenance ¶ This signet is a lesser work of shadow—neither one of the Nine nor a Ring of Power in its own right, but forged to harmonize with them . Smiths loyal to the Dark Lord cast it in the fumes of Orodruin’s fires, quenching the band in the chill of Morgul water and setting a black glass gem cut from the same volcanic obsidian used to edge Morgul blades. In ages past, Khamûl the Easterling bore rings that answered the will of the One; this signet remembers that cadence. It is a tuning fork for wraithdom , designed to steady death magic, reveal the half-seen, and—over days—pull its wearer across the veil. Appearance ¶ A lean, iron-dark band with hammered facets that never reflect warmth. The inner rim bears hair-fine gouges like teeth marks ; under moonlight they crawl into legible sigils The stone is a lens of night. Stare long enough and you’ll notice pin-prick lights moving far beneath , as if watching you back. The Temptation of Power ¶ The ring grows stronger the longer it is worn continuously (attuned and on your person). Stage I — Dormant: Immediately on attunement. Stage II — Stirring: After 3 consecutive days worn. Stage III — Ascendant: After 7 consecutive days worn. If you remove the ring for 24 hours or receive remove curse , drop one stage (min I). Favor of the Eye (Doing Sauron’s Bidding) ¶ When you complete a task Sauron explicitly commands through the ring (DM adjudicates), you may claim his Favor within 24 hours: - Instantly set the ring to Stage III (Ascendant) for 24 hours. - Boon: Until the next day, the undead you control have advantage on their first attack each combat and you may cast Danse Macabre and Shadow of Moil without using a spell slot. Shared Properties (All Stages) ¶ Shadow Anchor (1/long rest). Reaction when you take damage: you may move up to 10 feet , then become Shadowform until the start of your next turn— you can move through creatures/objects as difficult terrain and have resistance to all damage except radiant and force . While in Shadowform you can’t cast spells, make attacks, or take reactions . If you end inside an object, take 1d10 force and are shunted to the nearest space. Sacred Bane. You have vulnerability to radiant . While on holy ground (e.g., hallow ), you have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks . Stage I — Dormant ¶ Necromantic Aptitude I. +1 to spell attack rolls and damage with necromancy. Undead you control gain +1 to attack and damage rolls . Veil-Piercer I. Your darkvision increases by 30 ft. , and you can see through magical darkness . The Voice Whispers. Sauron can whisper to you —short, unmistakable messages the DM may deliver at any time (no action, any distance/plane). Stage II — Stirring ¶ (Includes Stage I benefits unless replaced.) - Necromantic Aptitude II. +2 to spell attack rolls and damage with necromancy. Undead you control gain +2 to attack and damage rolls . - Veil-Piercer II. While in dim light or darkness , you have see invisibility . - Grave Tether. When a creature drops to 0 HP from a necromancy spell you cast, gain temporary HP equal to your level/2 (once per turn, rounded up). - The Eye Turns. Sauron knows your general location (direction and within a few miles) while you wear the ring. - Taint of Shadow. You have disadvantage on Persuasion checks against good-aligned creatures and exude a faint, unsettling chill. Stage III — Ascendant ¶ (Includes Stage II benefits unless replaced.) - Necromantic Aptitude III. +3 to spell attack rolls and damage with necromancy. Undead you control gain +3 to attack and damage rolls . - Veil-Piercer III. Constant see invisibility ; in dim light/darkness you also gain blindsight 10 ft. - Wraith’s Command (1/short rest). Reaction: When a creature dies within 60 ft. , you may raise it as a Wight under your control for 10 minutes . It acts immediately after your turn, can’t create spawn , and counts against any control limits. When the duration ends, it crumbles to ash. - Sunlight Sensitivity. In direct sunlight, you have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight. - The Hand Commands (Geas of the Nine). After completing a long rest while wearing the ring, make a DC 21 Wisdom saving throw . On a failure, you cannot remove the ring and you are affected by geas (no further save) until the next day with a command delivered through the ring. Every hour you directly disobey the command, you take 2d10 psychic damage , and the DM may impose disadvantage on saves vs. charm and fear until your next dawn. The effect ends early if you complete the command, or the ring is targeted by remove curse cast with a 7th-level slot or higher.

In direct sunlight, you have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight. - The Hand Commands (Geas of the Nine). After completing a long rest while wearing the ring, make a DC 21 Wisdom saving throw . On a failure, you cannot remove the ring and you are affected by geas (no further save) until the next day with a command delivered through the ring. Every hour you directly disobey the command, you take 2d10 psychic damage , and the DM may impose disadvantage on saves vs. charm and fear until your next dawn. The effect ends early if you complete the command, or the ring is targeted by remove curse cast with a 7th-level slot or higher.

docs.text: Suvaria ¶ Converted from the original Homebrewery source into portable Markdown. View the published Homebrewery document . Welcome traveler from an antique land. Please sit and tell us of what you have seen. The unheard of monsters, who slither and bite. Tell us of the wondrous items and and artifacts you have found, their mysteries yet to be unlocked. Of the vexing vocations and surprising skills you have seen. Homebrew Rules ¶ Character Alignment - Please track your character alignment using the Ethics and Morality chart . During the game your DM may require you to make an Alignment Check for heroic or evil deeds. Potions - Drinking a potion requires only a bonus action. Force feeding someone else is an action. Drinking the same potion multiple times in succession may require a Constitution saving throw. Flanking - Works the same as Pathfinder 2e . A creature is flat-footed (taking a –2 penalty to AC) to creatures that are flanking it. Lingering Injuries - These injuries will depend on the damage that caused the player to crit fail a saving throw or take damage that brings them below 0 Hit Points. Examples: Minor - Things like broken bones may cause a movement or attack disadvantage until healed during a long rest or use Lesser Restoration to remove the condition. Major - If a limb is destroyed beyond repair you may need to use a prosthetic until you find a cleric powerful enough to cast Regenerate. Curses - Some curses will require special material components in addition to the Remove Curse spell. Spell Material Components - Any spell component worth less than 100 gold or below level 4 is kept in a material pouch and never needs to be resupplied. Item Attunement - When you receive a new magic item that requires attunement you can choose to instantly attune the item if you have an attunement slot available. Attuned items that are traded between party members still require a Short Rest to attune the item to the new owner. Wild Shape Languages - In addtion to understanding languages they know, a wild shaped druid can understand and speak to beasts of the same kind it has turned into as if using the Speak with Animals spell. New Character - Generally, if a player character remains dead or missing for an extended length of time they become an NPC. Consult the DM if you wish to die or play another character. Rule Clarifications ¶ Skills with Different Abilities - We are using this variant rule. Please ask your DM if you have proficiency with a skill and would like to use a different ability for: https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/basic-rules/using-ability-scores#VariantSkillswithDifferentAbilities Healing Spirit - We are using the 2020 Errata for Healing Spirit. It can only heal a number of times equal to 1 + your spellcasting ability modifier: https://www.sageadvice.eu/2020/04/01/xanathars-guide-everything-errata/ Polymorph - While polymorphed you can still identify friend or foe but can be influenced by animalistic urges. You only understand the languages listed in the creature’s stat block. Weapon Group Specializations ¶ Due to the rigorous daily practice it requires, you may only have one weapon group specialization at a time. You may retrain this using a week of downtime whenever you are in a friendly city. If you don't know if a weapon can be used with a specialization please ask your DM. Polearm Specialization: ¶ When you critically strike the target is moved up to 10 feet in a direction of your choice. This is forced movement. When you make an athletics check to shove a mounted foe you have advantage on any attempt to shove the rider off of its mount. Sword Specialization: ¶ When you critically strike the target is made off-balance by your attack, becoming flat-footed (-2 AC) to everyone until the start of your next turn. In place of an attack, you may use your sword to attempt to disarm an opponent of equal or smaller size by using an Athletics or Acrobatics check. Bow Specialization: ¶ If the target of the critical hit is adjacent to a surface, it gets stuck to that surface by the missile. The target is immobilized and must spend it's movement action making a DC 10 Athletics check to pull the missile free; it can’t move from its space until it succeeds. Reduce the AC provided by cover by one degree when attacking with a bow. Brawling Specialization ¶ When you critically strike the affected target’s speed is halved(minimum of 5ft) and it cannot take reactions until the start of your next turn. You have advantage on Attack rolls against a target you are Grappling. Axe Specialization ¶ When you critically strike, choose one creature adjacent to the initial target and within reach. You deal damage to that creature equal to the result of the weapon damage die you rolled. This amount isn’t doubled, and no other additional dice apply to this damage. You gain a +1 bonus to your attack roll if you already attempted to attack a different target this turn using this weapon. Club Specialization ¶ When you critically strike the affected target is knocked prone. You deal damage equal to your strength modifier when you make an athletics check to shove a target regardless of if you succeed. Dagger Specialization ¶ When you critically strike the affected target takes 1d8 persistent bleed damage. You gain an item bonus to this bleed damage equal to double the weapon’s item bonus to attack rolls. When you are wielding a dagger weapon, increase the base damage die size of that weapon by one step. Spells ¶ Note: Reward spells require no spell slot unless specified. Crowlies Cromatic Sparks ¶ transmutation spell Casting Time: 1 action Range: 120 feet Components: V, M, S (bit of glitter) Duration: Up to 3 hours Uses: 1 per short rest This spell is similar to skywrite except it works a lot better at night since it's just fireworks without the noise. You can also write on buildings and clothing. The smaller the writing the longer it lasts. The color of the sparks is affected by the color of the glitter used. Level 5 : Writing on a surface now lasts 24 hours and you can weave intricate shapes into your writing. Wild Shrooms ¶ conjuration spell Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet Components: V, M, S (dirt) Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Uses: 1 per long rest As an action, while in the forest or underground you touch the dirt and call upon the Mycelium spirits to come to your aid! Suddenly a ring of mushrooms up to 20ft in diameter appears in the designated location. Anyone that walks within a foot of the ring is affected by the mushroom's spores. The size and effects of the mushrooms are determined by what kind they are. (best start studying those now...) Level 5 : Assuming you have been casting this, you are now proficient in mushroom knowledge and have a better idea of what kind of mushrooms you are calling forth. Animated Shroom ¶ conjuration spell Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: 30 feet Components: V, M, S (dirt, mushroom spore) Duration: Up to 1 hour Uses: 1 per long rest As an action, you instantly grow and animate a mushroom that you control. The mushroom takes on the appearance and taste of whatever type of mushroom spore you used to animate it. The mushroom follows your instructions unless you tell it to do something stupid like jump off a cliff (it is intelligent after all). The mushroom is friendly and stays animated for 1 hour then reverts back into a regular mushroom. You can cast Animated Shroom on it again to reanimate and it will retain its memories from before. Stats (minus the sunlight sickness). https://5e.tools/bestiary/myconid-sprout-mm.html Level 7 : The mushroom gets stronger https://5e.tools/bestiary/myconid-adult-mm.html Eisenheim's Book of Illusions ¶ Note: Advanced spells only usable by illusionist wizards Illusory Creature ¶ Illusion spell, level 2 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 500 feet Components: V, S Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour You create an illusory image of a Large or smaller creature. It generates the appropriate sounds, smells, and feels believable to the touch. If you and the image are ever farther than 500 feet apart, the spell ends. The image can't speak, but you can use your actions to speak through the creature, with the spell disguising your voice as appropriate. You might need to attempt a Deception or Performance check to mimic the creature, as determined by the GM. This is especially likely if you're trying to imitate a specific person and engage with someone that person knows. In combat, the illusion can use 1 action per turn. It uses your spell attack roll for attack rolls and your spell DC for its AC. Its saving throw modifiers are equal to your spell DC – 10. It is substantial enough that it can flank other creatures. If the image is hit by an attack or fails a save, the spell ends. The illusion can cause damage by making the target believe the illusion's attacks are real, but it cannot otherwise directly affect the physical world. If the illusory creature hits with a Strike, the target takes psychic damage equal to 1d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier. This is a mental effect. The illusion's Strikes are nonlethal. If the damage doesn't correspond to the image of the monster—for example, if an illusory Large dragon deals only 5 damage—the GM might allow the target to attempt an immediate Perception check to disbelieve the spell. Any relevant resistances and weaknesses apply if the target thinks they do, as judged by the GM. For example, if the illusion wields a warhammer and attacks a creature resistant to bludgeoning damage, the creature would take less mental damage. However, illusory damage does not deactivate regeneration or trigger other effects that require a certain damage type. The GM should track illusory damage dealt by the illusion. Any creature that touches the image or uses the Seek action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. When a creature disbelieves the illusion, it recovers from half the damage it had taken from it (if any) and doesn't take any further damage from it. At Higher Levels: The damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd and the maximum size of creature you can create increases by one (to a maximum of Gargantuan). Blanket of Stars ¶ Illusion spell, level 4 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 500 feet Components: V, S Duration: up to 10 minutes A flowing cloak of utter darkness drapes over you, filled with pinpricks of light like distant stars. It imparts the stillness of the cosmos to you, granting you a +2 status bonus to Stealth checks to Hide and Sneak. While outside under a starry night sky, you're also invisible as long as you remain still. When moving under a starry night sky, you have Advantage on stealth checks instead. Gazing too closely into the stars is disorienting. Any creature that ends its turn adjacent to you must attempt a Wisdom save against your spell DC; this is a mental, visual effect. On Failure the creature rolls with disadvatage against you until the end of its next turn. Item Facade ¶ Illusion spell, level 1 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 10 feet Components: V, S Duration: up to 1 hour You make the target object look and feel as though it were in much better or worse physical condition. When you cast this spell, decide whether you want to make the object look decrepit or perfect. An item made to look decrepit appears broken and shoddy. An intact item made to look better appears as though it's brand new and highly polished or well maintained. A broken item appears to be intact and functional. Destroyed items can't be affected by this spell. A creature that Interacts with the item can attempt to disbelieve the illusion. Shadow Projectile ¶ Illusion spell, level 2 Casting Time: 1 reaction Range: 120 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instant You create an illusory duplicate of your ally's ranged attack to confuse your opponents. You launch an illusory double of your ally's projectile or spell at the same target, leaving the enemy unsure which attack to avoid. Target must attempt a Wisdom save against your spell DC. On failure, the target takes 3d8 psychic damage and your ally may roll their attack with Advantage. Regardless of the result of its save, it's temporarily immune to shadow projectile spells for 1 hour. Curses and Boons ¶ Curse of Loviatar (Krunk) ¶ The Maiden of Pain has placed a curse on you making every injury you receive more enjoyable. After a long rest roll a d6, the effect lasts until your next long rest: 1. Nothing happens, you feel as if the curse is weakening. 2. You wake up to find you have stabbed yourself in your sleep somehow, 2d6 damage. 3. First time you are dealt damage in a combat encounter by a melee attack you must make a Wisdom Saving Throw(DC 14). On a fail, you spend your next action attempting to convince your attacker to hit you again and gain resistance to all physical damage. 4. You wake up with a back is covered in welts that toughen your skin. Decrease damage taken by 1d4 for the day. The welts make you vulnerable to Poison Damage. 5. You feel like you stepped on a nail but when you look nothing is there. Reduce movement speed by 10ft due to limp for the day. 6. You wake up and discover you have a painfully large hook body piecing on your head that sharpens your senses. Reduce max health by 1d10 and gain +2 to Consitution Saving Throws. Items ¶ Maul of Maelstroms (Caracus) ¶ Maul, uncommon (requires attunement) You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The bonus damage is lightning damage. Once per long rest you can shout a battle cry and slam an enemy dealing an extra 1d10 thunder damage. They must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be knocked back 10ft and prone. You feel a slight shock whenever you pick it up, the weapon seems to vibrate with energy Ring of the Gladiators (Krunk) ¶ Wondrous item, common Explosive applause every time you crit to attack or deliver a killing blow to an enemy. Add 1d6 to your next attack roll. Laugh track if the wielder crit-fails on an attack roll. Subtract 1d6 to your next attack roll. Gilly's Bag of Beans (Caracus?) ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon |#| Color | Effect | |:----:||:----:|:-------------| |1.| Yellow | Ipicac | |2.| Purple | Eagle | |3.| Green | Bear | |4.| Red | Bull | |5.| Blue | Cat | |6.| Grey | Owl | |7.| Brown | Fox | |8.| Black | Unknown | As a bonus action you may eat or give a bean. Most of these beans Enhance Ability but several do other things. Make a Intelligence check (DC 12) to pick the correct bean. On a fail, roll a d8 and use that to select the color. The duration is 10 minutes. Party currently has 20 beans. Gilly warns only to eat one bean per person before taking a rest. Ring of Charm (Bells) ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon 3 charges per day. You may cast Charm Person (DC 15) but you must shake the targets hand(with your ring hand) in order to do so. The target does not learn you tried to charm it on the first usage regardless of success or fail. Eyes of the Eagle (Ella) ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon While wearing them, you have advantage on Perception and Investigation checks that rely on sight. In conditions of clear visibility, you can make out details of even extremely distant creatures and objects as small as 2 feet across. Boots of Elvenkind (Vex) ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon While you wear these boots, your steps make no sound, regardless of the surface you are moving across. You also have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks that rely on moving silently. Veil of Shadows (Krunk) ¶ Wondrous item, rare A large black amulet also known as Shield of the Void. Once per day you can use a Bonus Action or a Reaction to speak this amulet's Command Word to create an aura that lightly obscures and gives resistance to all damage types until your next turn to everything in a 10 ft radius around you. Sword of Screams (Krunk) ¶ Longsword, uncommon When pulled from it’s scabbard everyone within 60ft of it is deafened for 1d4 turns. It has the same stats as a Longsword and is magical. While weilding this weapon you may ask DM the to play selected screamo or metal music. Helm of Invisibility (Ella) ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon This helmet that makes the wearer's head invisible. You may use this helm once per day to give yourself Advantage on an Intimidation or Deception check. Talking Skull (Bells) ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon This skull has forgotten its name and seems to be constantly eyeing you. Once per day you can animate the skull, lighting up its eyes with a pale blue light. Roll a d6 and a d100. While animated it speaks with you and will answer a question to the best of its ability if you correctly guess a riddle. Garland of Garlic (Caracas) ¶ Net, uncommon A magical garland of garlic laced with silver barbs. On hit, it wraps around the vampirie's neck and prevents it from using its bite action. Cannot be removed or destroyed by a vampire regardless of shape changing. Has the same properties as a Net except it does not restrain. Bone Breaker (Caracus) ¶ Mace, uncommon (requires attunement) A large spiked mace that says “Bone Breaker, do not use!” hastily written across it. 1d6 bludgeoning, +1 piercing, +1 to hit, is Magical - Break Bones (Recharge 5-6): Melee Attack, on hit the target must succeed a Constitution Save(DC 14) or have their AC reduced by 1 and speed reduced by 10ft until healed. - Hunger for Blood: At the start of combat the wielder must make a Wisdom Save(DC 14). On fail, you must dash and Reckless Attack(Barbarian) an enemy within melee range of Bone Breaker. - Bloodied Rage: While the wielder is bloodied in combat this weapon deals an extra 1d4 bludgeoning damage. At the start of his turn the weilder must make a Constitution Save(DC 14) to avoid attacking the nearest creature (random if more than one adjacent). Chilling Halberd (Krunk) ¶ Halberd, uncommon (requires attunement) You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon and can apply the Call of the Grave affect when you hit. - Call of the Grave (Recharge 6): Add 1d6 Necrotic Damage, a ghostly skeletal hand attaches to the target and they can’t regain hit points until the start of your next turn. Until then, the hand clings to the target. If you hit an undead target, it also has disadvantage on its next attack roll against you until the start of your next turn. Shadow Dagger (SOLD) ¶ Dagger, rare (requires attunement) You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. - Returning: Shadow Dagger returns to the wielder’s hand immediately after it is used to make a ranged attack. - Backstabber: Roll an addtional 1d4 damage when the target is flatfooted. - Create Undead Minion (Long Rest): Once per long rest you may spend an action to stab the Shadow Dagger into a fresh corpse. The corpse becomes an undead minion and obeys your commands until it is destroyed or you use this ability again. (high CR creatures will be reduced to one) Demon Mask (SOLD) ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon This terrifying mask is crafted in the visage of a leering demon and grants a +1 item bonus to Intimidation checks. - Leering Gaze (Long Rest): The mask casts the fear spell with a DC of 14(or spell bonus) on a single target that can see it. This doesn't require concentration of the wearer. Shield of Friendship (???) ¶ Wondrous Sheild, uncommon As a bonus action, you may send your shield to another creature (1) up to 30ft away, giving them +2 AC until the start of your next turn. Until the sheild returns you do not benifit from it's bonus. If your hands are full at the start of your turn the sheild appears at your feet or in a holster you are wearing. Horschopper (???) ¶ Wondrous Guisarme, uncommon You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. This magical makeshift +1 Guisarme can be weilded with one hand but deals 1d6 instead of 1d10 when attacking someone 10ft away Necklace of lightning bolts (Strawberry) ¶ Wondrous Guisarme, uncommon Once per turn, you can use an action to detach a bead. When you do a 3rd-level Lightning Bolt spell (save DC 14) is created in the direction of your choice. You can detach multiple beads, or even the whole necklace, as one action. When you do so, increase the level of the Lightning Bolt by 1 for each bead beyond the first. You may use this while wildshaped if the creature has enough manual dexterity. Kinesis Module (Ella) ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon (requires attunement) Kinesis Grab: As an action, you can cast Mage Hand . The spectral hand created by this spell is invisible. Kinesis Launch (Recharge after a Short Rest): Once per short rest, you can cast Catapult at the 4th level without using a spell slot (6d8). The damage dealt by this ability can be modified by the item you choose to throw. The Kinesis Module, inspired by Dead Space, grants the wielder telekinetic abilities. This magical item is perfect for tactically minded characters who wish to manipulate their environment and use objects as weapons in creative ways. Plasma Cutter of Limb Severance (Caracus) ¶ Weapon (ranged), uncommon (requires attunement) Damage: 1d10 radiant Properties: Range (40/120), ammunition (battery, 30 shots), light, two-handed Limb Targeting: When you make an attack with this weapon, you can choose to target a limb (arm, leg, wing, etc.) of a creature that has them. You have a -2 penalty to the attack roll, but on a hit, the attack deals an additional 1d10 radiant damage. You may only do this once per turn. Severing Beam: On a critical hit against a limb, the limb is severed if it is a type that can be severed, causing additional effects at the DM's discretion (like reduced movement speed for a severed leg). Battery: The weapon has 30 shots before its battery needs to be recharged or replaced. This ranged weapon, modeled after the plasma cutter from Dead Space, is designed for precision targeting of limbs. It offers a unique tactical advantage, allowing characters to disable foes effectively at range. Stasis Module Charm (Bells) ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon (requires attunement) Charges: It holds 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. Usage: As an reaction, you can expend one charge to cast the Slow spell on a single target within 30 feet, without requiring concentration or Saving Throw. The effect lasts until the start of the targets next turn. Flavor: The charm emits a brief blue light and a low hum when activated, and the targeted creature appears to move in slow motion. The Stasis Module Charm, inspired by the Stasis Module from Dead Space, is a small device that can momentarily slow time around a specific target. It brings a tactical advantage, allowing the wielder to hinder a powerful foe or control the battlefield's tempo. Ash's Righteous Chainsaw Blade (Krunk) ¶ Weapon (greatsword), rare (requires attunement by a Paladin) Damage: 2d6 slashing + 2. (1d6+1 unactivated) Properties: Heavy, two-handed. Special: On a critical hit against undead, the blade deals an additional 2d8 fire damage. The fire symbolizes the purifying flame against the undead. Chainsaw Roar: Once per combat on your turn, the wielder can activate the chainsaw as a free action. Everyone within 60ft becomes deafened until the end of start of your next turn. In addition, any enemy you attack this turn must make a DC 14 Wisdom save or be Frightened until the start of your next turn. Chainsaw: Anything made of wood is vulnerable against this weapon. This magical chainsaw sword, made by Ash Williams' iconic weapon from the Evil Dead series, melds the brute force of a greatsword with the visceral power of a chainsaw. Spiked Shield: (SOLD) When you use the shove action and succeed you may use this sheild to deal 1d4 + Strength piercing damage. It gives a permanent +1 to Charisma skill checks (not impacted . It also allows the user to cast "Comprehend Languages" once per day without using a spell slot. Once per long rest, the wearer can cast the "Mending" spell on a broken historical document or magical artifact (may require a DC check). Vengeful Packmate (New Adult Trait) * Having grown alongside its Oath of Vengeance paladin, Lucifer has developed a fierce protective streak.* If a creature deals damage to an ally on their turn, Lucifer has advantage on attack rolls against that foe until the end of the blink dog’s next turn. When your proficiency bonus increases by 1 the bonuses to hit and damage of its Bite attack increase. Actions ¶ Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. 10(2d6 + 3) magical piercing damage. Teleport (Recharge 4-6). Lucifer magically teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to its movement speed, to an unoccupied space it can see. Lucifer can use blink as the spell, and can evoke or end the effect as an Action Dimension Door (Recharge after Long Rest). Lucifer can create a dimension door as an Action. Time to Drop Knowledge ¶ The blink dog is an intelligent canine that takes its name from its ability to blink in and out of existence, a talent it uses to aid its attacks and to avoid harm. Blink dogs harbor a long-standing hatred for displacer beasts and attack them on sight. Culture: Blink dogs tend to live in closely knit packs consisting of related individuals. Much like wolves, these packs are generally comprised of a family unit--a mother, a father, and their children. Unlike wolves, it is not uncommon for a pack to also include extended family members (grandparents, aunts, uncles) and the adult children of the pack, which are welcome to stay and expand the pack by bringing home a mate. Language: Blink dogs have their own language, a mixture of barks, yaps, whines, and growls that can transmit complex information. Combat: Blink dogs hunt in packs, teleporting in a seemingly random fashion until they surround their prey, allowing some of them to take advantage of flanking. Maturation Rate: Blink dogs will mature into an adult at about 10 months(at which point ask me for a new sheet). Warranted Suspicion: Blink dogs tend to be highly suspicious of other races, as the wicked and unscrupulous have long sought their fortune by stealing blink dog pups with the intention of "taming" and "training" them and then selling them for outrageous amounts of coin. Given that blink dogs are sapient creatures the equal of any human, dwarf, or elf, this practice is understandably viewed by blink dogs as kidnapping and slavery. docs.text: Character Alignment - Please track your character alignment using the Ethics and Morality chart . During the game your DM may require you to make an Alignment Check for heroic or evil deeds. Potions - Drinking a potion requires only a bonus action. Force feeding someone else is an action. Drinking the same potion multiple times in succession may require a Constitution saving throw. Flanking - Works the same as Pathfinder 2e . A creature is flat-footed (taking a –2 penalty to AC) to creatures that are flanking it. Lingering Injuries - These injuries will depend on the damage that caused the player to crit fail a saving throw or take damage that brings them below 0 Hit Points. Examples: Minor - Things like broken bones may cause a movement or attack disadvantage until healed during a long rest or use Lesser Restoration to remove the condition. Major - If a limb is destroyed beyond repair you may need to use a prosthetic until you find a cleric powerful enough to cast Regenerate. Curses - Some curses will require special material components in addition to the Remove Curse spell. Spell Material Components - Any spell component worth less than 100 gold or below level 4 is kept in a material pouch and never needs to be resupplied. Item Attunement - When you receive a new magic item that requires attunement you can choose to instantly attune the item if you have an attunement slot available. Attuned items that are traded between party members still require a Short Rest to attune the item to the new owner. Wild Shape Languages - In addtion to understanding languages they know, a wild shaped druid can understand and speak to beasts of the same kind it has turned into as if using the Speak with Animals spell. New Character - Generally, if a player character remains dead or missing for an extended length of time they become an NPC. Consult the DM if you wish to die or play another character.

docs.text: Illusion spell, level 2 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 500 feet Components: V, S Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour You create an illusory image of a Large or smaller creature. It generates the appropriate sounds, smells, and feels believable to the touch. If you and the image are ever farther than 500 feet apart, the spell ends. The image can't speak, but you can use your actions to speak through the creature, with the spell disguising your voice as appropriate. You might need to attempt a Deception or Performance check to mimic the creature, as determined by the GM. This is especially likely if you're trying to imitate a specific person and engage with someone that person knows. In combat, the illusion can use 1 action per turn. It uses your spell attack roll for attack rolls and your spell DC for its AC. Its saving throw modifiers are equal to your spell DC – 10. It is substantial enough that it can flank other creatures. If the image is hit by an attack or fails a save, the spell ends. The illusion can cause damage by making the target believe the illusion's attacks are real, but it cannot otherwise directly affect the physical world. If the illusory creature hits with a Strike, the target takes psychic damage equal to 1d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier. This is a mental effect. The illusion's Strikes are nonlethal. If the damage doesn't correspond to the image of the monster—for example, if an illusory Large dragon deals only 5 damage—the GM might allow the target to attempt an immediate Perception check to disbelieve the spell. Any relevant resistances and weaknesses apply if the target thinks they do, as judged by the GM. For example, if the illusion wields a warhammer and attacks a creature resistant to bludgeoning damage, the creature would take less mental damage. However, illusory damage does not deactivate regeneration or trigger other effects that require a certain damage type. The GM should track illusory damage dealt by the illusion. Any creature that touches the image or uses the Seek action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. When a creature disbelieves the illusion, it recovers from half the damage it had taken from it (if any) and doesn't take any further damage from it. At Higher Levels: The damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd and the maximum size of creature you can create increases by one (to a maximum of Gargantuan).

docs.text: The blink dog is an intelligent canine that takes its name from its ability to blink in and out of existence, a talent it uses to aid its attacks and to avoid harm. Blink dogs harbor a long-standing hatred for displacer beasts and attack them on sight. Culture: Blink dogs tend to live in closely knit packs consisting of related individuals. Much like wolves, these packs are generally comprised of a family unit--a mother, a father, and their children. Unlike wolves, it is not uncommon for a pack to also include extended family members (grandparents, aunts, uncles) and the adult children of the pack, which are welcome to stay and expand the pack by bringing home a mate. Language: Blink dogs have their own language, a mixture of barks, yaps, whines, and growls that can transmit complex information. Combat: Blink dogs hunt in packs, teleporting in a seemingly random fashion until they surround their prey, allowing some of them to take advantage of flanking. Maturation Rate: Blink dogs will mature into an adult at about 10 months(at which point ask me for a new sheet). Warranted Suspicion: Blink dogs tend to be highly suspicious of other races, as the wicked and unscrupulous have long sought their fortune by stealing blink dog pups with the intention of "taming" and "training" them and then selling them for outrageous amounts of coin. Given that blink dogs are sapient creatures the equal of any human, dwarf, or elf, this practice is understandably viewed by blink dogs as kidnapping and slavery. Curious Companions: Although most blink dogs keep strictly to their own kind, some eccentric individuals chose to attach themselves to roving "packs" of adventurers, spurred on by curiosity.
